title: ATT&CK technique map (Google Doc)
description:
Amaka: 'The board sees this map with your name on it. Wrong technique IDs make us look careless to anyone who reviews this. Map each observed behaviour to the MITRE ATT&CK technique that describes it, and justify each pick with the evidence line that supports it.'

**Submission via Google Doc link.** A mapping is a table; tables don't render in the writeup pad. Create a Google Doc, set sharing to **'Anyone with the link → Viewer'** (we will not chase access requests), and paste the URL below with a 50+ word abstract.

**Required structure in the Doc — one table with these columns:**

| # | Observed behaviour | Evidence (file path or `tab:timestamp`) | MITRE technique ID | Technique name (verbatim from attack.mitre.org) | Justification (1 sentence) |

**Required rows (in this order — 6 mandatory):**

  1. SSH login from external IP using a valid public key for `o.adegoke`.
  2. The Griot's use of `less` over `/var/log/*` to obtain a root shell via interactive shell-escape.
  3. Sourcing `/var/lib/mc/.helper` from `o.adegoke`'s `.bashrc` on every new shell.
  4. Periodic HTTPS beacons to `gri0t-c2.dynamic-update.net`.
  5. Use of HTTPS (TCP 443) over the standard egress proxy as the C2 channel.
  6. Initial recon — `id`, `uname -a`, `ls /home`, `cat ~/.bashrc` in the bash history.

**Add two more rows of your own choosing from the artefacts** — pick non-obvious ones (e.g. forensic-evading by not modifying timestamps; the use of an existing legitimate user account to mask the attacker). **8 rows total.**

**Source-of-truth — every technique ID must come from a current `attack.mitre.org/techniques/T...` page.** ID + name must match the canonical entry exactly. Use the search at https://attack.mitre.org/.

**Citation bar:**
- All 8 technique IDs in current MITRE ATT&CK form (`T1078`, `T1548.003`, `T1546.004`, `T1071.001`, `T1568`, `T1059.004`, etc.). Made-up IDs or paraphrased names lose 4 pts each.
- Quote the full technique name as MITRE writes it.
- For at least one row, name the MITRE D3FEND counter-technique that mitigates the technique (`https://d3fend.mitre.org/`).

**Evidence appendix in the Doc:** list every artefact you cited in the table by full path or `tab:timestamp`.

**One mistake I almost made:** 40+ word section in the Doc. The seductive wrong answer is mapping persistence to `T1543 Create or Modify System Process` (systemd-style persistence) when this evidence is clearly the shell-config sub-technique under `T1546.004`. Explain why you nearly mismapped.

**Minimum 400 words in the Doc (table content counts) + the 8-row table.** Paste the link + 50+ word abstract below.

---

**Universal grading rule.** Generic answers fail. Every claim in your submission must be tied to specific evidence — an artefact from the lab (file path, log line, command output, payload, screenshot) **and** at least one external citation where research is relevant (NIST section number, MITRE technique ID, CVE, vendor advisory, ISO control ID, NDPA section). Claims without an attached artefact, timestamp, payload, standard section, or business constraint earn zero for that claim. Lab-only answers earn partial credit. External-only answers earn partial credit. Full credit requires both.
